result.title: What Not to Erase: Saliency-Constrained Augmentation for Low-Resource Handwritten Character Recognition
result.summary: Optical Character Recognition (OCR) and handwritten character recognition (HCR) in low-resource historical material collections often rely on data augmentation, yet augmentation strategies are typically evaluated almost exclusively through predictive accuracy. This leaves open whether a model's improved performance is accompanied by saliency stability. This question is important in low-resource historical HCR, where recognition is performed on variable and partially degraded letterforms and two models with similar predictive performance may differ in how consistently their saliency patterns respond to such variation. We therefore study saliency-guided augmentation as an explanation-aware strategy for low-resource HCR. Rather than treating saliency maps only as post-hoc interpretations, we use them to define augmentation variants that perturb, preserve, or constrain visually informative regions of character images. We compare classical document-style transformations, random lacunae, and several saliency-constrained lacuna variants. To evaluate the effect of augmentation beyond accuracy, we introduce the Explainability Consistency Index (ECI), a metric that quantifies the stability of saliency patterns under controlled perturbations. We find that saliency-constrained augmentation can improve recognition over classical augmentation, but no single saliency strategy is consistently best. The preferred form of the constraint varies with both architecture and corpus, indicating that saliency is better treated as a mechanism for controlling augmentation than as a fixed augmentation strategy. In some settings, saliency-constrained training improves explanation consistency even when predictive performance is similar. This shows that predictive metrics alone can obscure differences in model sensitivity under perturbation, motivating explanation consistency as a complementary evaluation dimension.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究低资源历史手写字符识别中的增强策略：用 saliency map 定义扰动、保留或约束字符图像中信息区域的多种 lacuna（人为缺损）增强，并提出 Explainability Consistency Index 量化受控扰动下 saliency 模式的稳定性；结果显示受约束增强可优于经典增强，但最优约束形式随架构与语料而变化，且性能相当时解释一致性仍可能不同。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「扰动下显著区域稳定性」评价思路可能为检验 LVR 内部状态是否稳定保留任务必要视觉细节、区分准确率相近但视觉证据依赖不同的模型提供可供核查的启发，但该指标能否迁移到多模态推理仍需验证。
